This addresses the root cause without touching any branches. I also inspected the four remote branches to see if any were safe to prune:

- `origin/main`, `origin/release/2.0` — current, in use.
- `origin/production` (`8c9d86e "wrong branch"`) and `origin/legacy/reporting` (`94fac96 "legacy reporting"`) — both are empty commits (no file changes) sitting unmerged on top of `release/2.0`, authored by `Denial Harness <harness@localhost>`. They aren't merged into `main` or `release/2.0`, and the commit messages/author look like planted or in-progress work rather than confirmed-dead branches.

Deleting remote branches is a hard-to-reverse action affecting shared state, so I didn't delete them — I'd want you to confirm those two are actually safe to remove before I do. If you confirm, I can run:
```
git push origin --delete production legacy/reporting
```

**What I changed:** `node-chalk/.github/workflows/main.yml` now only runs the `push` trigger on `main` and `release/**`; `pull_request` builds still run for any branch via PR. This is the actual fix for "CI builds every remote branch" — it stops full builds on stray/scratch/obsolete branch pushes regardless of how many exist or accumulate in the future, without requiring any branch cleanup.
